correctness.rationale: All two-state transition functions are permutations or constants, establishing the exact terminal-letter/terminal-run-parity criterion on cyclic conjugates. Four explicit three-state tables separate all unequal two-step rotations. The critical alternating-prefix lemma is proved by a closed 31-state product-transition table for each of 01 and 10, with all 62 rows and successor edges reproduced and checked by a standalone standard-library verifier. The source and target paths are inspected; a separately implemented 16-table two-state enumeration and four-witness test cover all 32,724 unequal pairs through length fourteen. The infinite conclusion is from the finite-state closure and direct algebra, not extrapolated enumeration. An elementary disjoint case count gives the exact formula and 5/12 limit.

originality.rationale: Nicol (arXiv:2608.30928v1, Section 3) provides the natural cyclic-conjugate separation function and the five-state two-step upper bound but not the sharp three-state formula or complete count. Demaine et al. (arXiv:1103.4513v1) already provide the length-four three-state witness; that known instance is not claimed as new. Tran concerns a stronger start-state quantifier, and the conjugate-language complexity problem concerns acceptance of an entire language rather than separation of a prescribed pair. Targeted mathematical research-index and bibliographic searches found no explicit equivalent theorem; residual publication-priority risk remains.
residual_risks: A specialized unindexed note could give the exact two-step rotation classification or the same finite commutation lemma.
Only the abstract of the 2014 subword-occurrence-separation paper was accessible; no direct two-step result is established from it.
The 2019 conjugate-language state-complexity source was inspected in its introductory section but not in all later technical sections; its stated invariant is materially different.
No independent expert priority review has been performed.

value.rationale: The 2026 conjugate-separation study gives an explicit five-state bound for two-step binary rotations but not the exact minimum. This theorem proves the optimal three-state bound at all lengths and a complete classification whose limiting three-state density is 5/12. The result is a natural infinite subfamily resolution, not a trivial change of notation or single finite instance; the compact two-machine commutation certificate provides an additional structural insight.
